subject: Proposal: convertible ramp tranche + auto-renew opt-out / true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@brightwellhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightwellhealth.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase — initial ask

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Hope you’re both well. We’re beginning our renewal conversations for Brightwell and expect to increase monthly token consumption by ~40% across Q4/Q1 as we roll out a new feature. Procurement asked I share an initial request so we can align on term structure and cadence:

- Prefer a 24-month commitment to get a lower unit rate, but we need staged capacity: 60% of new capacity year 1 and the remainder ramping in months 13–18.
- Would like an auto-renew opt-out window (60 days) rather than automatic extension without notice.
- True-up: monthly true-up with ability to add a short-term top-up (single-digit % flexibility) if we spike.
- We’ll need a documented SLA credit mechanism for sustained latency regressions (production SLOs are non-negotiable).

Attached: Brightwell_renewal_request_Q3.pdf with estimates and current usage profile. Can we book 30 minutes this week to sketch options? Ideally include pricing and legal-friendly redline guidance.

Thanks — Asha
Asha Patel
Director, Product
Brightwell Health

Attachment: Brightwell_renewal_request_Q3.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — initial ask

Thanks Asha — good context. I can do a quick sketch and recommend two pragmatic paths before legal:

1) 24-month convertible tranche (preferred):
   - Year 1: committed baseline + 60% of incremental capacity staged as you described.
   - Year 2: remaining incremental capacity available as reserved units with predictable unit pricing.
   - Monthly true-up; annual reconciliation with a capped glide-path to avoid bill shock.

2) 12-month + optional 12-month extension (flex):
   - Lower commitment length but higher nominal unit price; includes an explicit opt-in extension window at month 9.

For the auto-renew opt-out, we can implement a 60-day written notice with a one-time grace that protects against accidental auto-renew if procurement misses the window. On SLO credits: we can offer a defined credit ladder (severity/time-based) but need product to sign-off on measurable latency buckets — Marissa, can you confirm acceptability on our standard SLO tiers or escalate?

Proposed time: Thu 09/02 10:00 PT — 30 minutes to align on direction. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach a high-level quote.

– Jonas
VP, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@brightwellhealth.com>, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — initial ask (pricing sketch)

Asha — appreciate the details. After modeling the usage profile I put together two concrete quotes (attached) and added operational guardrails below.

Quick summary (see attached quote-Brightwell-v2.xlsx):
- Option A (24mo convertible tranche): effective unit rate $0.0068/token for committed baseline + staged incremental banding: 60% ramp in months 1–12 billed monthly; remaining 40% available at locked rate months 13–24.
- Option B (12mo + 1yr extension opt-in): effective unit rate $0.0076/token baseline; extension triggers require written acceptance at month 9.

Operational mechanics we recommend:
- Monthly true-up with a 10% tolerance band before automatic top-up billing; above that we trigger an Ops review and offer a one-time soft top-up (30 days) to avoid throttling.
- Auto-renew opt-out window: 60 days notice; include a 14-day “safety-repeat” that sends procurement a reminder at 30 days.
- SLO credits: we can commit to a three-tier credit ladder (P1/P2/P3) with a maximum annual credit of 2% ARR unless a repeated systemic regression is identified.

Attached: quote-Brightwell-v2.xlsx, SLA-exception-request-form.pdf (fill & return if you need custom SLO wording). If Option A is preferred I’ll convert to a formal amendment and mark the staged capacity schedule for legal redline.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Accounts — Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quote-Brightwell-v2.xlsx (xlsx), SLA-exception-request-form.pdf (pdf)

From: Asha Patel <asha@brightwellhealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightwellhealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase — initial ask (we prefer Option A)

Thanks Marissa — Option A looks closest to what we want. A couple of clarifications before we route to procurement/legal:

- True-up cadence: monthly true-up with the 10% tolerance band is acceptable. For top-ups, we want explicit language that a top-up cannot exceed 15% in any single month without written approval from our procurement lead.
- Auto-renew: agree to 60-day opt-out window + reminder cadence. Please include the reminder language in the amendment.
- SLO credits: the 2% ARR cap is OK as a starting point, but we need an escalation path if regressions repeat within a 90-day window (escalation to product + engineering).

Procurement has asked for a clean quote and an editable amendment we can redline. Can you send the amended contract language + DocuSign link and I’ll push to our procurement queue?

Asha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: approval band for SLO credit + draft amendment items

Internal note — looping here to confirm what we can approve before legal:

- Approved: a one-time annual SLO credit cap at 2% ARR for intermittent regressions. If the customer requests an escalation path for repeated regressions within 90 days, we can promise a formal review and priority engineering triage but only approve incremental credits after product signs off (we should avoid open-ended credit liabilities).
- For the convertible tranche: approve the staged ramp schedule as described by Marissa. Finance asks that we include a clear early-exit true-up calculation (pro-rated usage vs committed at a 120% protection multiplier). We should include an optional escrowed-onramp clause that allows Brightwell to pre-purchase a small buffer (3 months of incremental capacity) to smooth spikes.

Next steps: Marissa — please produce the editable amendment with the reminder language for auto-renew, the top-up cap (15%), and the escrowed-onramp addendum. I’ll provide a short authorization note for legal to expedite review.

– Karthik
SVP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
